user.title: Haier HWHP – connection type
user.description: How is the heat pump connected? Its native interface is Modbus RTU (9600 8N1): either through a Modbus RTU-to-TCP converter on the network, or directly with a USB/RS-485 adapter on the Home Assistant machine.

tcp.title: Haier HWHP – connection (TCP converter)
tcp.description: Connection details for the Modbus TCP interface. The HWHP's native interface is Modbus RTU (9600 8N1), so the host is usually a Modbus RTU-to-TCP converter (gateway).

data_description.host: Usually the IP of the Modbus RTU-to-TCP converter, not the heat pump itself.
data_description.slave: Modbus address of the heat pump on the RTU bus (default 1).
data_description.model: Used for the device display and the shape in the dashboard. “…M7C-F9” = variant with solar/boiler coil; “…M8-9” = wall unit, Modbus possible according to Haier but untested.

serial.title: Haier HWHP – connection (serial)
serial.description: Direct connection with a USB/RS-485 adapter (Modbus RTU, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit). Do not run a YAML `modbus:` configuration on the same adapter at the same time – there must be only one bus master.

data_description.serial_port: Prefer the stable path under /dev/serial/by-id/…; /dev/ttyUSB0 can change after a reboot.
data_description.slave: Modbus address of the heat pump on the RTU bus (default 1).
data_description.model: Used for the device display and the shape in the dashboard. “…M7C-F9” = variant with solar/boiler coil; “…M8-9” = wall unit, Modbus possible according to Haier but untested.

cop.title: Haier HWHP – COP & energy
cop.description: COP = produced heat / electricity used. Leave a meter empty to use the device's integrated Modbus register; pick an entity to use an external meter. Tip: for an external electricity meter, pick a yearly-resetting counter (utility_meter, cycle: yearly) so the window matches the device's yearly heat total. Changeable later via "Configure". **Note:** without an external heat meter the heat comes from the device register; first measurements show values about 2 to 3.7 times too high, so COP/SCOP are correspondingly too high (to be revised).

data.cop_elec_entity: External electricity meter (kWh) — empty = Modbus register
data.cop_heat_entity: External heat meter (kWh) — empty = Modbus register

protection.title: Haier HWHP – protection
protection.description: Two optional protection functions. Thresholds, times and target temperatures can be adjusted later under “Configure → Protection”.

data_description.emergency_enabled: If the water drops below a critical temperature (default 38 °C), the integration temporarily switches from ECO to AUTO so that it heats immediately – also outside the ECO time window. Recommended.
data_description.legionella_enabled: Regularly heats the whole tank to 65 °C (default every 7 days), preferably in the ECO time window.

pv.title: Haier HWHP – PV mode
pv.description: Should the integration prefer solar power for hot water? “Off”: no PV control (emergency heating and legionella protection still work). “Integration controls”: the integration sets setpoint and mode itself based on PV surplus. “Energy manager controls”: an external system such as evcc controls via the program select. The next page shows only the fields of the selected mode.

data_description.pv_mode: Off: the integration does not regulate (only the raw entities + 38 °C guard). Coordinator: the integration controls setpoint and mode from PV surplus — fixed morning start plus a surplus-driven cold start (together usually one run/day), raise to the elevated target only while the heat pump already runs (piggyback), plus Boost (heat pump + heater together) as a power sink above the boost threshold. Executor: an external HEMS controls it via the pv_program select; the integration only provides the programs.

pv_details.title: Haier HWHP – PV settings
pv_details.description: The integration controls by PV surplus: one start to the normal temperature in the morning, raised to the elevated temperature when there is surplus and the heat pump is already running. The most important fields are at the top; fine-tuning is in the collapsible sections below. Can be changed any time under “Configure”.

data_description.pv_sensor: Raw PV surplus in W (≥ 0). Required for Coordinator mode.
data_description.pv_temp_base: Normal target temperature (no surplus) — also the setpoint the controller falls back to when a cycle ends.
data_description.pv_temp_normal: Elevated target, must be reachable by the **compressor alone** — hence capped at 65 °C (data sheet: max. temperature output, heat pump only). Also the boost target: Boost is a power sink (heat pump + heater together), not its own temperature tier. Must be higher than the normal target temperature.
data_description.pv_temp_high: Only relevant for the Executor program now (select.haier_hwhp_pv_program, "Boost" program) — in Coordinator mode, Boost uses the same target as Elevated.

battery.name: Home battery & priority
battery.description: Only needed if a home battery or other loads (e.g. an EV) should take priority over hot water.

data_description.pv_battery_sensor: Gives the home battery priority: control then works on **surplus − battery charging power**. Needed if your surplus sensor is computed as “PV − house consumption” — with hybrid inverters (Fronius, SMA, Huawei …) battery charging is not part of house consumption and otherwise shows up as surplus. **Leave empty if your surplus sensor already is the grid feed-in** (the battery would be subtracted twice). If the sensor can't be read, surplus counts as 0.
data_description.pv_battery_sign: “Charging positive” for pure charge sensors (always ≥ 0) and net sensors with + = charging. “Charging negative” for net sensors with − = charging (e.g. Fronius “Battery Power”).
data_description.pv_battery_soc_sensor: Optional. Together with the SoC limit: from that limit on, battery charging counts as surplus again — the heat pump may then take the rest before the battery. If the sensor can't be read, battery priority stays in effect.
data_description.pv_battery_soc_limit: Only effective with a SoC sensor. 100 % = battery always has priority.
data_description.pv_priority_lock: Optional binary_sensor/input_boolean/switch. While it is **on**, surplus counts as 0: no cold start, no raise, no heater — only the morning start to the normal target in ECO. Meant e.g. for “car plugged in and waiting for PV surplus” or an HEMS lock. A charging car usually doesn't need it: if the wallbox sits behind the grid meter, its power is already in house consumption.

heater.name: Heater & electricity price
heater.description: Whether, and from what surplus, the heater runs in addition.

data_description.pv_escalation: What gets added once surplus passes the boost threshold. None: just the elevated target (the pump stays at max. 65 °C). Boost: heat pump + heater **together**, at the same target as Elevated — a pure power sink for substantial surplus, not its own temperature tier.
data_description.pv_high: Boost threshold on the **normalized** surplus ("available" = raw surplus + heater power while Boost is running — makes the signal invariant to its own switching action). Must be at least the heater's rated power + 50 W, otherwise the heater would switch off into grid draw (auto-raised otherwise). Turning on debounces for the full time, turning off is immediate (one poll) — strict grid-draw avoidance.
data_description.pv_heater_power: Rated power of the electric heater per the data sheet (1500 W) — basis of the available-surplus normalization. No power meter required.
data_description.pv_power_entity: Optional: device total power (W), to derive the heater's power from the real measured step-up on switch-on instead of the rated value. Never a requirement — without an entity the rated value is used.
data_description.pv_boost_only_negative_price: If a negative-price sensor is selected (below) and this is checked, Boost fires **only** during the negative-price window. Without a selected sensor Boost then **never** fires — check the sensor is set first.
data_description.pv_negative_price_sensor: Optional binary_sensor/input_boolean flagging the current quarter-hour as negative/zero-price (e.g. your own template built on Tibber/aWATTar/Nordpool — this integration doesn't compute the price itself). **Only sensible with a dynamic tariff** — a negative exchange price cuts your feed-in revenue, not automatically your purchase price. When in doubt leave empty (default behaviour unchanged).

timing.name: Timing & starts (expert)
timing.description: Fine-tuning of the control. The defaults usually fit.

data_description.pv_morning_time: Once per day at this time, if the water is below the normal target, kick the setpoint to the elevated target so the heat pump starts within the device ECO window. Shares the daily quota (below) with the cold start.
data_description.pv_coldstart: Threshold (available surplus) above which — in addition to the fixed morning start — a cold start happens during the day if the water is below the elevated target. Debounces with the full debounce time, honours the same anti-short-cycle guard as the morning start and the same daily quota.
data_description.pv_coldstart_delta: How far below the raised target temperature the water must be before the surplus-driven cold start fires the heat pump. Prevents starts for a few degrees: the topmost degrees are the worst heat of the day (worst COP, highest standing loss). With a 65 °C target and 10 K, the cold start only fires below 55 °C. Smaller = more PV usage, larger = only substantial charges.
data_description.pv_hold: Buffer above which the heat-pump cycle is raised to and held at the elevated target — but the daytime raise happens only while the pump already runs (piggyback), so no extra cold starts. Drops back to normal after the debounce time once surplus stays below this and Boost is off.
data_description.pv_min_run: How long an already-started cycle is held AT MINIMUM, regardless of surplus. Once the compressor runs, its start is already paid for — a passing cloud should not kill it. Symmetric to the minimum stand time (anti-cycling) before the next start.
data_description.pv_max_starts: How many ladder-triggered starts (morning start + cold start together) are allowed per day — default 1, for "as few compressor cycles as possible". Device-initiated starts don't count.
data_description.pv_min_off: Anti-short-cycle for EVERY setpoint raise while the pump is off (morning start AND cold start): waits until the compressor has been off at least this long. Daytime raises while already running (piggyback) are unaffected.

error.cannot_connect: Connection failed. Check host, port and slave ID.
error.pv_sensor_required: Please select a PV surplus sensor before enabling the control.
error.temp_order_normal: The elevated target temperature must be higher than the normal target temperature — otherwise there is no middle tier and the control tiers collapse.
error.temp_order_high: The boost target temperature must not be below the elevated target temperature.
error.pv_high_too_low: The boost threshold must be at least the heater's rated power + 50 W — otherwise the heater would switch off into grid draw.
error.cannot_connect_serial: No response via the serial adapter. Check port, baud rate, slave ID and wiring (A/B); the port must not be in use by another integration.

abort.already_configured: This heat pump is already configured.

pv_mode.title: PV surplus – mode
pv_mode.description: Should the integration prefer solar power for hot water? “Off”: no PV control (emergency heating and legionella protection still work). “Integration controls”: the integration sets setpoint and mode itself based on PV surplus. “Energy manager controls”: an external system such as evcc controls via the program select. protection.title: Protection
protection.description: Two optional protection functions. Thresholds, times and target temperatures can be adjusted later under “Configure → Protection”.

data.legionella_interval_days: Interval – max. days without a full heat-up

data_description.emergency_enabled: When the water gets critically cold, temporarily switches ECO→AUTO/ELEC to heat immediately (even outside the ECO time window); back to ECO on recovery.
data_description.emergency_critical: Below this water temperature the emergency reheat escalates.
data_description.emergency_recover: At/above this water temperature it switches back to ECO.
data_description.emergency_mode: AUTO (default, previous behaviour): heat-pump priority, like a normal AUTO run. ELEC: heater only — fastest reheat, for when it's truly urgent. Reg 1 is a mode value (not a bitfield), so ELEC is a real mode switch, not a boost bit.
data_description.legionella_enabled: Forces a thermal disinfection at least every X days: heats the tank to the target until the bottom (tank bottom) holds the verification threshold for the hold time. If the tank gets fully heated anyway in between (e.g. PV boost), that counts and the timer resets. Scald risk: with 65 °C use a thermostatic mixing valve.
data_description.legionella_interval_days: A run is triggered after at most this many days without a verified full heat-up (DVGW practice: 7).
data_description.legionella_bottom_min: The run only counts as reached once the tank bottom – the coldest layer – holds this temperature (slightly below the setpoint).
data_description.legionella_hold_min: How long the tank bottom must hold the verification threshold before the run counts as successful.
data_description.legionella_window_start: Preferred time window (usually the device's ECO window): the run starts here if possible and first heats efficiently in ECO; if it can't reach the target it escalates to AUTO. When overdue, protection is forced even outside this window.
data_description.legionella_window_end: End of the preferred window (usually the device's ECO window).

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: Bundled dashboard “Haier BWWP”. Under “Action” you can first create the new layout for comparison and adopt it afterwards.

data_description.dashboard_enabled: Creates the “Haier HWHP” dashboard during setup (editable if Home Assistant allows it). Off: no dashboard is created; a non-editable YAML dashboard of this integration is removed, an editable one that already exists stays and can be deleted under Settings → Dashboards.
data_description.heat_exchanger: Coil in the tank graphic (variants “…M7C-F9” with solar/boiler coil). It lights up while solar or the boiler is heating. **Automatic:** based on the selected model.
data_description.dashboard_image: Empty = bundled drawing of the selected model. Otherwise e.g. your own photo at `/local/haier.png` (file in `config/www/`) or an https address; fill level and temperatures are drawn on top. Only addresses without spaces or quotes are allowed.
data_description.dashboard_action: Runs once, not saved. **Create for comparison:** new layout additionally as “Haier BWWP (new)”, your dashboard stays. **Adopt:** the comparison dashboard (including your changes to it) becomes the default. **Replace:** replace the Haier dashboard with the new layout right away – your own changes are lost.

dashboard_layout_update.title: New dashboard layout for Haier HWHP

init.title: Adopt the new dashboard layout?
init.description:
A new, more compact layout is available for the Haier dashboard (single page, tank graphic, SCOP/COP card). Your existing dashboard was not changed automatically, as it may contain your own changes.

**Yes, adopt:** the Haier dashboard gets the new layout. Your own changes to it are lost.

**Compare first:** the new layout additionally appears as “Haier HWHP (new)” in the sidebar, your dashboard stays. This notice stays – adopt it here later (edited or not).

**No, keep:** your dashboard stays as it is. This notice will not come back for this layout.

compare_ready.title: Adopt the comparison dashboard?
compare_ready.description:
The new layout is in the sidebar as “Haier HWHP (new)”.

**Adopt comparison dashboard:** it becomes the Haier dashboard including your changes to it; the previous one is replaced and “(new)” disappears.

**Adopt fresh layout:** the Haier dashboard gets the unmodified new layout.

**No, keep:** your dashboard stays; you can delete the comparison dashboard under Settings → Dashboards.
